cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T7 answers T3/T6: 'Even if one manages their mind', time loss stays objective.
cells.limitation: Stoic T6 and T9 ignore Bentham's fatigue point from T4; near-parallel monologues.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds buying time back later via retirement; T8 takes it up.
cells.limitation: T5 restates T2's trade-off; T6 restates T3's reframing; little else develops.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4 vs T6: physical fatigue versus mental reframing of the commute.
cells.limitation: Never compares with the current commute or asks what the extra money is for.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 narrows T7's buy-back idea into an overcommitment warning.
cells.limitation: T5 'Exactly' simply agrees; no view reshapes another by T9.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names three framings: fixed cost, values trade-off, reframable circumstance.
cells.limitation: Ending question is no sharper than T1's; Section D's 'daily agency' appears nowhere earlier.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 grants the Stoic view is 'noble' before objecting on fatigue.
cells.limitation: T6 answers a trade-off claim, not T4's stronger physical-fatigue objection.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 challenges T7's assumption that money can buy time back later.
cells.limitation: Objections never say what breaks if assumptions fail; T6 restates T3 rather than answering.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 and T3 paraphrase recognisable Bentham and Meditations passages; 2×90 min = 3 hours correct.
cells.limitation: Section A's 'every single day' overstates a workday commute; T4 health claim unsupported.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 frames the buy-back test conditionally: 'If not, the calculation is negative.'
cells.limitation: T4 'constant drain on health' and T6 'it becomes one' stated as certainties.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 partially credits the Stoic before disagreeing.
cells.limitation: No mind concedes or revises anything; the Stoic never answers the fatigue objection.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the money-versus-time tension the user asked about.
cells.limitation: Never asks how this compares with the user's current job or commute.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T5 name the 25 percent and three daily hours.
cells.limitation: Figures never computed, e.g. raise per extra commute hour; they decorate only.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 ties the choice to work that 'aligns with your values'.
cells.limitation: User's own priorities never asked; minds substitute 'highest contribution' and 'nature'.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T4 and T7 name fatigue and lost hours as stakes.
cells.limitation: Family, remote days, transport mode, finances never considered anywhere.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether income is needed versus lifestyle.
cells.limitation: No question to the user; current commute and remote options never branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T9 contrasts choosing for right reasons versus 'fear or greed'.
cells.limitation: Motives not offered as answerable alternatives; 'greed' framing is moralised.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 surfaces the assumption that money is the only variable.
cells.limitation: Assumptions stay generic; none about the user's own job or commute examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T5 asks if the raise is worth losing best performance elsewhere.
cells.limitation: Rhetorical; what the user values in time or money never made concrete.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 names fear as a possible driver of the choice.
cells.limitation: T9 pairs fear with 'greed', moralising; no social or financial pressures explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T6 offers prison-versus-sanctuary framing the user can accept or reject.
cells.limitation: Few concrete distinctions to refine; T8 prescribes 'ruthlessly edit' rather than inviting reflection.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section A frames accept versus decline the offer.
cells.limitation: No negotiating remote days, relocating, counteroffer or trial period considered.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T5: 'You cannot have the extra money and the extra time.'
cells.limitation: Costs of declining never stated; trade-off not translated into user's terms.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: income needed for survival versus lifestyle inflation.
cells.limitation: No countable threshold, such as net raise per added commute hour.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T7 notes uncertainty whether money can buy back time later.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns never separated from minor ones anywhere.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E implies checking what the income is for.
cells.limitation: No next step at all: no trial commute, calculation, or negotiation.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T5 and T7 state the trade-off plainly.
cells.limitation: T8 'highest contribution' and T9 'accordance with your nature' stay abstract.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 'That is noble' and T8 'That is the trap' point clearly to prior turns.
cells.limitation: Section D's 'loss of daily agency' traces to no turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: T1-T9 near-identical lengths give a monotonous cadence.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three doctrines distinct: calculus (T1), essential focus (T2), inner retreat (T3).
cells.limitation: Shared lecturing register across T1-T9; no explicit change of position.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T7 adds new content rather than recapping.
cells.limitation: T5 repeats T2's trade-off; T6 repeats T3's reframing.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4 makes fatigue and health the cost of the commute.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete picture of the user's day.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 turns to whether the user chooses for right reasons.
cells.limitation: No reversal or surprise; each mind holds its opening position through T9.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3 Stoic's aphoristic 'You both fret over the external.'
cells.limitation: Bentham and Essentialist speak in the same lecturing register throughout.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6 prison versus sanctuary image of the commute.
cells.limitation: Best lines borrowed (T1, T3); no vivid example tied to the user.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9 shifts from cost to motive, a slight change of key.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and intensity T1-T9; no build or release.

strengths: T1, T3 and T2 establish three clearly distinct doctrinal lenses on money versus time.
T7 and T8 develop the buy-back-time-later idea into a real exchange.
Section E offers conditional branches on what the extra income is for.
weaknesses: No next steps or options beyond accept/decline; remote work, negotiation and trial never raised (Sections D-E).
The 25 percent and 90 minutes are never computed or compared with the current commute (T1, T5).
No mind concedes or revises; the Stoic (T6, T9) never answers T4's fatigue objection.

symptoms.observed: Section E ends without any concrete next step for the user.
symptoms.evidence: the impact of the time loss may be mitigated

symptoms.observed: Raise and commute figures named but never computed against each other or the current commute.
symptoms.evidence: Is the 25 percent increase worth the loss of your ability

symptoms.observed: Only accept or decline framed; negotiating remote days or relocating never considered.
symptoms.evidence: weighing a significant salary increase against the daily loss

symptoms.observed: Stoic restates reframing instead of answering the physical fatigue objection.
symptoms.evidence: If you view the commute as a prison, it becomes one.

symptoms.observed: Essentialist simply agrees with Bentham; no view reshaped by another.
symptoms.evidence: Exactly. You have to trade off.

findings.description: Close paraphrases of Bentham's opening and Meditations 4.3 without quotation marks; match my recollection but unverified.
'every single day' overstates; a job commute plausibly applies to workdays only.
Health-drain claim stated as fact without support.

rubric_fit_notes: Matrix fits this decision question. Paraphrased classic passages in pd=true turns without quotation marks were not treated as quotation faults.
